1. QC task-token release: DID fail, but not as anticipated. RunQualityControl failed after only ~12s with TaskFailed (resource "invoke.waitForTaskToken"), not TaskTimedOut. Cause: ValueError: parameter=<event> has no type hint | cannot infer event type — raised inside calendar_qc/main.py's _build_agent() when constructing the Strands Agent with hooks=[_ToolCallBudget(...)]. Strands' hook auto-registration calls get_type_hints() on the raw hook object when it isn't a HookProvider; an instance has no __annotations__ of its own (those live on its bound __call__), so type inference failed and the ValueError propagated up through run_qc's except-block, which correctly reported it to Step Functions via report_to_step_functions(token, error=exc) before re-raising — so the TaskFailed behavior (vs. a timeout) is actually the exception path working as designed. The rest of the chain fell through the States.ALL catch exactly as this bead predicted, and QC was silently skipped for the week even though the state machine reported SUCCEEDED.

   Fixed by making _ToolCallBudget implement the HookProvider protocol (register_hooks(registry) explicitly calling registry.add_callback(BeforeToolCallEvent, self._on_before_tool_call)) instead of relying on implicit type-hint inference over the instance. handler.py's get_cors_origin() now returns None (no ACAO header) for any origin outside ALLOWED_ORIGINS instead of falling back to '*'; add_cors() and the OPTIONS preflight both skip the header entirely when there's nothing to allow. Added test_handler.py covering allowlisted/unrecognized/missing-origin cases for both the direct helper and the OPTIONS branch. All 386 api tests pass.

While verifying live against the deployed API, found the same wildcard leak one layer up: api_stack.py's UNAUTHORIZED/ACCESS_DENIED gateway responses (API Gateway's own 401/403 for requests the Cognito authorizer rejects before Lambda runs) hardcoded Access-Control-Allow-Origin: '*' unconditionally — that path never goes through handler.py at all. Fixed by reflecting the caller's own Origin header (method.request.header.origin) instead of a literal wildcard; gateway responses can't run a real conditional allowlist check the way get_cors_origin() does, and these bodies are low-sensitivity (fixed "Unauthorized"/"Forbidden" text, no user data), so reflection here is a reasonable compromise that also keeps the legitimate dctech.events admin frontend able to read a 401 to show "please log in" rather than getting an opaque CORS failure.

- /api/admin/corrections (401 via Cognito authorizer, gateway-response path): with cache-busting query strings (CloudFront — API Gateway EDGE endpoints sit behind an AWS-managed CloudFront distribution — was serving a stale cached copy of the pre-fix 401 for identical repeated URLs, which is expected default error-caching behavior and not a real residual issue), evil origin now gets its own origin reflected (not a blind '*'), dctech.events gets its own origin reflected, and a request with no Origin header at all gets no ACAO header.

Added packages/calgen/src/calgen/ssrf_guard.py (safe_get) and wired it into calendars.py's two external fetch points: fetch_json_ld_data (Meetup page scraping) and fetch_ical_and_extract_events (group iCal feeds). Validates the resolved IP before connecting and rejects private/loopback/link-local/multicast/reserved/unspecified addresses (covers the metadata endpoint 169.254.169.254, localhost, RFC1918 ranges, etc).

Also closes the DNS-rebinding gap explicitly: the validating wrapper (a scoped socket.getaddrinfo patch) stays installed through the whole request, including requests/urllib3's own connection-time resolution and each redirect hop it manually follows — not just an up-front check — so a DNS answer that changes between the check and the actual connect is still caught rather than sailing through on the second, unguarded lookup.
